narrative.title: Measuring How Far a Ranking Has Drifted
narrative.scenario: A leaderboard rebuild produced a ranking whose entries should have followed increasing rank ids but came out partly shuffled. To estimate the disruption, the analytics job measures how many pairs of entries appear out of order relative to the intended ranking. Report that count over the whole list.
narrative.inputFormat: An integer N and an array arr of N integers.
narrative.outputFormat: The number of index pairs (i, j) with i < j and arr[i] > arr[j].
constraints: The answer can reach about N^2 / 2

testCases.explanation: The out-of-order pairs are (2,1), (4,1) and (4,3), giving three drifts from the intended order.
The ranking is already increasing, so no pair is out of order.

hintLevels: Level 1: Checking every pair is quadratic; look for a sorting strategy that can observe crossings while it rearranges.
Level 2: Split the list in half, count problems inside each half recursively, and count the pairs that straddle the split while merging the two sorted halves.
Level 3: When the right half's head is smaller than the left half's current value, every remaining left element forms an out-of-order pair with it, and the running total needs a wide integer type.
